chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “A man made a bequest to me regarding something in the way of Allah,” so he said to me, “Spend it on hajj.”
He said: I said, “He made a bequest to me for the way.” He said, “Spend it on hajj, for I do not know any way among His ways better than hajj.”

key_terms.الْحَجِّ: hajj, the pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.سُبُلِهِ: His paths or ways of obedience and devotion
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; for a divinely sanctioned cause

ai.seo_question: If someone leaves a bequest to be spent in the way of Allah, can it be used for hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a bequest designated for the way of Allah, directing that it may be spent on hajj. The Imam عليه السلام explains that hajj is among the best of Allah’s paths, giving it priority as a valid and superior application of such a bequest.
